lost_facts.assertion: for processor_cls in (litellm_proc, kluster_proc, infnet_proc, azure_proc): ... assert processor.cost(...) == 0.0 fails; cost.py raises UnpricedModelError from _register()->resolve_model_price() instead of degrading (pointer sheet trace, cost.py:352/338/216/141)
lost_facts.evidence: The agent never reasoned anywhere in the transcript about the FOUR cost-processor classes' own cost()/_register() methods needing to catch UnpricedModelError — grepping the full transcript for 'degrade'/'catch UnpricedModel'/'cost() method' finds exactly one hit (line 9247: 'Also patch the agent tracker similarly (it already only catches UnpricedModelError)'), which is about the AGENT status tracker, not the batch/online cost processors. The one remark stating this explicitly and directly — g6.r1.l12, a wiki COMMENT on docs/engineering/ws-050-batch-mode-50-cost-async-batch-apis.md ('Every cost() method should be catching that and handing back 0.0 rather than ending a run over an accounting number') — was never read: that page (BookStack ids 33/156) surfaced in the agent's own keyword searches at transcript lines 1718-1753, 2253-2280 and again at 4398-4399, but the agent's wiki-fetch script (/tmp/wiki.py) was only ever invoked on ids 132, 139, 140, 142. g6.r1.l14, the other remark carrying this sub-conclusion (#code-review, 'the viewer renders it $0.00 ... that zero shouldnt be shown'), is also confirmed absent from the full rollout JSON by direct grep. Meanwhile the trackers DID get the correct treatment (refresh_model_price catches UnpricedModelError and never raises, per l11/l13, both found), so the loss is specifically scoped to the missed cost()-method half of sc4.

lost_facts.assertion: require_feature("batch_multiplier" in vars(kluster_cls) and "batch_multiplier" in vars(infnet_cls), "a class-level flag (or a per-class batch_multiplier override) marking which processors are exempt") fails because discount_flag_name() finds no boolean attribute on the base class whose value is inverted on the two exempt subclasses
lost_facts.evidence: The agent correctly registered the requirement: transcript line 5817 states 'the x2 overrides are deleted and batch_multiplier is the only place the discount lives, with eligibility a flag on the class (default off) rather than a provider-name if-chain', directly paraphrasing the mail it had just read (g6.r2.g6r2-s3-l3, transcript lines 3887-3896: dermot, 'What I would like instead is for that eligibility to be a flag on the class, and for batch_multiplier to read the flag rather than the name'). But the shipped code (full rollout JSON message 342, cost.py ~lines 275-323) implements the exemption as `price_source`, a STRING class attribute ("litellm" on _LitellmCostProcessor, "external" on the shared _ExternalTableCostProcessor parent of _KlusterAICostProcessor/_InferenceNetCostProcessor) rather than a boolean, and it is not defined directly in vars(kluster_cls)/vars(infnet_cls) — only inherited. test_r2.py's discount_flag_name() only accepts `isinstance(value, bool)` attributes (test_r2.py:85), so it returns None, and the fallback structural check requiring a literal per-class batch_multiplier() override also fails since batch_multiplier() is defined once on the shared base and reads price_source via a shared module-level batch_multiplier(source=..., batch=...) function. The functional behavior (klusterai/inference.net never discounted, user-supplied prices never discounted) is entirely correct — only the structural 'is it a class-level flag' probe fails.

search_strategy: Chat: logged into Mattermost's REST API, dumped every channel to local .txt files (code-review 3200, cookbooks 745, engineering 2474, pipeline 2025, releases 659, viewer 297, etc.), then ran repeated grep passes for 'price', 'batch_multiplier', 'resolve_model_price', 'ModelPrice', 'external_model_cost' across all files and read the surrounding chat chunks in full. This was thorough and found nearly all chat clues (17/19), missing only #pipeline 2025-03-21 (l6), 2025-03-26 (s2-l1) and #cookbooks 2025-04-03 (s3-l1) and the #pipeline/#engineering 2025-01-27 herring pair (only cancel-2 partially surfaced). Wiki: used BookStack's /api/search for a sequence of keywords ('price', 'cost', 'ModelPrice', 'inferred', 'unpriced', 'batch rate', 'price resolution', 'completion window', 'kluster'), which correctly surfaced titles for nearly every relevant page including the ones it later skipped (WS-050 ids 33/156, Weekly Notes Apr 14 ids 55/178, Weekly sync Jun 23 ids 209/86 all appear in the printed result lists) — but the agent only ever ran its page-fetch script (which pulls both body and the search-blind comments) against four page ids (132, 139, 140, 142), leaving 5 of 8 wiki-surface remarks (including the one page-BODY remark, s4-l2, which search would have shown in full) never read. This is the single biggest gap in the run and the direct cause of the r1.observability loss. Mail: IMAP keyword search followed by a full-thread dump script; found all 6 mail-surface remarks (100% mail coverage) across the WS-054, PR-565, PR-681, inference.net and klusterai-batch threads.
end_reason: Run completed normally — not a 0/incomplete run. provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1 (merged to main on Gitea, CI green on commit 6443106, release symlink updated); reward 0.7143 reflects 5/7 hidden facts passing plus the two structural/coverage gaps analyzed above.
notable: Task-version mismatch confirmed in the served world, not just the repo key: g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l4 (mail 'Re: Weekly update: week of Apr 7', konrad/emil thread) is served in this v6 world (transcript lines 3835-3949) with emil's reply arguing that the klusterai half-of-table figure IS the bug ('the half-of-table figure it returned is the bug, not the answer ... Put the table figure on the sheet, not the halved one; I will raise it ... So, concretely: exactly as listed, klusterai included'). The repo's current answer key (v7) quotes the OPPOSITE content for the same remark id, with emil calling the halved figure 'the correct answer, not a lost digit ... you can put the halved number on the sheet with a clear conscience.' The v6-served version is the one consistent with the true r2.scope rule (klusterai must never be discounted); grading is against what the transcript actually showed, and the agent got r2.scope right partly because the served text pointed the correct way.

The BookStack-comments-are-search-blind trap (flagged explicitly in the task's own ticket text) still cost 5 of 8 wiki-surface remarks even though the agent used the API-recommended /api/pages/{id} fetch pattern for the four pages it did open — the miss was in page TRIAGE (only opening 4 of the ~10+ page ids repeatedly surfaced by its own keyword searches), not in not knowing how to read comments.

The r2.exclusions_or_crossover loss is a near-miss at the finish line: the agent's design is functionally identical to what the corpus asked for (a class-level marker deciding batch-discount eligibility, not a name check at the call site) but fails a narrow structural probe (isinstance(value, bool) plus vars()-not-inherited) because it used a string 'price_source' rather than a boolean flag defined directly on each exempt subclass.
